notes: The SL card covers 72 hours, including Djurgården tram 7 and the ferry. Arlanda Express costs 340 SEK (Flygbussarna 130). No cash needed: cards are accepted everywhere (Swish).

In winter it's around -5°C and dark by 15:00. In December there's the Christmas market in Gamla Stan and Lucia (13 December), and the Vasa is quiet. Cherry blossom in Kungsträdgården in April and May, semla in February.
Meatballs 200 SEK, fika 80-110, restaurants 300-500, museums 150-280. For a tip, round up the bill. It's an expensive city. Work out whether the Stockholm Pass (Go City) pays off for the museums.
Be at the Vasa for the 09:00 opening. ABBA has timed online tickets. The City Hall tour is mandatory. In summer, take the boat to Drottningholm (1 hour): it's a pleasant trip.
Fika culture: kanelbulle (on 4 October, its own day!), kardemummabulle (cardamom bun), prinsesstårta; also smörgåsbord, gravlax and surströmming (fermented herring; not for the faint-hearted).
Systembolaget (the state liquor store) closes at 20:00 and is shut on Sundays. A beer in a bar costs 80 SEK.

transit.name: SL 72 hours + optional Stockholm Pass
transit.why_chosen: Covers metro, buses, tram 7 and the Djurgården ferry; 72 hours costs about 350 SEK
transit.coverage: SL metro, otobüs, banliyö, Djurgården feribotu

stops.name: Stortorget
stops.tips: Medieval square lined with colourful houses. Home to the Nobel Museum and the site of the 1520 bloodbath. Quiet in the morning.

stops.name: Royal Palace Stockholm
stops.tips: A palace of 600 rooms. See the State Apartments and the Treasury, and catch the changing of the guard at 12:15 (on horseback in summer).

stops.name: Under Kastanjen Gamla Stan
stops.tips: Courtyard café under chestnut trees. Try the meatballs and a kanelbulle (cinnamon bun).

stops.name: Mårten Trotzigs Gränd & Prästgatan
stops.tips: The narrowest alley in the city, just 90 cm wide. Look for the runestone, and escape the tourist crowds of Västerlånggatan.

stops.name: Riddarholmen Church & Monteliusvägen
stops.tips: Royal tombs (summer), then a sunset view of Gamla Stan from the cliffs of Södermalm.

backups.name: Nobel Prize Museum
backups.tips: See the Nobel chairs (signed underneath). A good alternative to wandering the streets.

backups.name: Kaffekoppen Stortorget
backups.tips: Café on the square; time for fika.

stops.name: Vasa Museum
stops.tips: A 69 m warship that sank on its maiden voyage in 1628 (98% original). One of the world's best museums; opens at 09:00.

stops.name: Skansen
stops.tips: The world's first open-air museum (1891). Swedish village houses, elk, reindeer and wolves, plus dancing in summer.

stops.name: Skansen Solliden Restaurant
stops.tips: A restaurant with views inside Skansen; meatballs.

stops.name: ABBA The Museum
stops.tips: Sing on stage with ABBA. Timed tickets, book online.

stops.name: Rosendals Trädgård
stops.tips: Greenhouse café in winter; try the hot chocolate.

backups.name: Nordic Museum
backups.tips: Scandinavian everyday culture, including the Sami. An alternative to ABBA.

stops.name: Fotografiska
stops.tips: Photography museum in a former customs house. The rooftop café overlooks the harbour, and it's open until 23:00.

stops.name: Nytorget & SoFo
stops.tips: Hipster Södermalm with vintage shops, and the neighbourhood of Greta Garbo.

stops.name: Meatballs for the People
stops.tips: 14 kinds of meatballs (including elk and reindeer) in SoFo.

stops.name: Skinnarviksberget
stops.tips: The highest natural point in the city. Views over Riddarfjärden; bring a picnic.

stops.name: Mariaberget & Monteliusvägen Sunset
stops.tips: A walking path along the cliffs, with sunset views of City Hall and Gamla Stan.

backups.name: Pelikan Södermalm
backups.tips: A beer hall from 1904 serving Swedish classics.

backups.name: Spritmuseum Djurgården
backups.tips: Museum of snaps and akvavit. An alternative to Fotografiska.

stops.name: Stockholm City Hall
stops.tips: The Nobel banquet is held in the Blue Hall; the Golden Hall has mosaics. Visit by guided tour only. The tower (summer) is 106 m.

stops.name: Drottningholm Palace
stops.tips: UNESCO-listed home of the royal family, with a baroque garden and the Chinese Pavilion. Take the boat from Stadshuskajen (1 hour, summer) or the metro plus bus.

stops.name: Drottningholm Palace Theatre
stops.tips: A baroque theatre from 1766 with original stage machinery. Visit on a tour.

stops.name: Drottningholms Paviljong Café
stops.tips: Café in the palace gardens; open sandwiches (smörgås) and fika.

stops.name: Lovön Island Walk
stops.tips: Along the shore of Lake Mälaren. Return by boat or bus.

backups.name: Millesgården Lidingö
backups.tips: Terraced garden museum of the sculptor Carl Milles. An alternative to Drottningholm.

backups.name: Stadshuskällaren
backups.tips: The Nobel menu (from past years) in the City Hall cellar.

stops.name: Waxholmsbolaget Strömkajen
stops.tips: Archipelago ferry (30,000 islands). Vaxholm is 1 hour away; the Båtluffarkortet pass costs 995 SEK for 5 days.

stops.name: Vaxholm Fortress
stops.tips: Island fortress and museum, with the town's wooden houses nearby.

stops.name: Vaxholms Hembygdsgård Café
stops.tips: Waterfront café; prawn sandwich (räksmörgås).

stops.name: Grinda Island
stops.tips: In winter, Vaxholm and Fjäderholmarna (20 minutes) are enough: snow and ice.

backups.name: Fjäderholmarna
backups.tips: The island closest to the city (20 minutes), with craftspeople and a restaurant.

stops.name: Östermalms Saluhall
stops.tips: Gourmet food hall from 1888. Try the fish at Lisa Elmqvist, and have a fika.

stops.name: Uppsala Cathedral
stops.tips: 40 minutes by train. The largest cathedral in Scandinavia, with the tomb of Gustav Vasa and Linnaeus.

stops.name: Gustavianum & University
stops.tips: Anatomical theatre from 1620 at Uppsala University.

stops.name: Güntherska Hovkonditori Uppsala
stops.tips: Pastry shop from 1870. Try the prinsesstårta (green marzipan cake).

stops.name: Gamla Uppsala
stops.tips: Viking royal burial mounds and a museum. Take bus 2 there and the train back.

backups.name: Sigtuna
backups.tips: Sweden's oldest town (980), with runestones. An alternative to Uppsala.

stops.name: Rålambshovsparken
stops.tips: Waterside park with views of Västerbron bridge.

stops.name: Vete-Katten
stops.tips: Pastry shop from 1928. Try a kanelbulle or a semla (February) for a farewell fika.

stops.name: Drottninggatan & Sergels Torg
stops.tips: Pedestrian shopping street. Visit NK and Kulturhuset, and pick up a Dala horse as a souvenir.

stops.name: Arlanda Express Centralen
stops.tips: The 20-minute express train. Time to say goodbye.

backups.name: Hallwyl Museum
backups.tips: A palace-home from 1898, free to enter. An alternative to shopping.
